page: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSv2 family, designed for workloads requiring massive memory capacity and high core counts. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors with an x86_64 architecture, this server features 416 vCPUs mapped to 208 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 5700.0 GB of RAM, providing approximately 13.7 GB of memory per physical core, alongside 8389 GB of local storage. The system runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the bottom 25%, the massive core count enables top-tier multi-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core benchmark and Passmark CPU score both rank in the top 10%. Memory performance is exceptionally strong, with cached small-block read bandwidth reaching 19406.65 GB/sec and uncached large-block read bandwidth at 767.47 GB/sec. Database operations are highly efficient, as demonstrated by Redis SET operations achieving 260.18 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M416s_v2 represents a high-density resource allocation suited for enterprise-scale consolidation. The massive memory footprint and high multi-threaded throughput justify its hardware class for specialized, memory-intensive applications. It is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory analytics engines, massive parallel data processing, and high-throughput web serving. However, it is less optimal for workloads dependent on high single-threaded clock speeds or real-time LLM text generation, where its performance is comparatively weak.
